comment.body: Thanks for the information already provided about Always on top fails to pin powershell properly when another command line program is running, then finishes. The report depends on an old PowerToys build and a custom command whose window and process transition may be central to the failure; current-version behavior is unknown. Please retest on the latest PowerToys release with a minimal command that launches and exits a child console process, provide the numbered sequence and whether the orphaned frame still appears, then add a comment containing `/bugreport` immediately after reproducing.

I believe this may be because it detects the other command line program and pins that instead, and when the command finishes, the console is the same, so it…
Reported result: The console disappeared, leaving the window controls
Expected result: The application to close properly without error
